thread:
alex: @maria heads-up — AcmeHealth POC streaming failing behind their corporate proxy. They see a 502 then the token stream stalls (tokens stop mid-response). Repro steps they gave below.

maria: Can you paste the logs and say if this is Hosted or Dedicated?

alex: Hosted. Using our TS SDK in an Electron renderer, HTTP(S)_PROXY set to their CAS proxy. Error shows `ECONNRESET` during streaming, sometimes `502 Bad Gateway` from the proxy, then long hang. Token stream stops after ~3–5s. Request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Model: mosaic-v1-7b.

dan: Do we know client-side timeouts and retry config?

alex: Defaults. They set no explicit fetch timeout and rely on streaming. Tried both our SDK and raw node-fetch. Also tried switching to our Python SDK in their backend — slightly better but still flaky.

jen: Quick check: I proxied a curl through a test CAS and saw chunked transfer stop after proxy closed the upstream connection at ~5s. Proxy likely kills idle upstream connections or buffers chunks.

dan: Common mitigation: enable keep-alive at the client, use an HTTP agent with keepAlive:true, and increase read timeouts. For Node: `new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs: 60000 })` and set `Connection: keep-alive`. Also make sure HTTP/1.1 is used (some proxies handle HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming better than HTTP/2 with buffering).

maria: On our side, hosted runtime will close an idle client after 30s — not matching 5s. So likely proxy-level behavior or TLS inspection. If proxy does TLS MITM / TLS intercept, it can buffer or terminate chunked streams.

alex: Sales question from customer: if they need to re-request partial responses because of stalls, how does billing work? Will they be charged twice for overlapping tokens?

maria: Billing counts tokens emitted by the model. If you re-request and cause overlapping generations, you'll be billed for both outputs. There's no automatic dedupe for streaming restarts today. For large overlap workloads this can increase cost.

dan: Workarounds: 1) Move the call to an internal backend service outside Electron so proxy rules differ. Python requests/urllib3 are often more tolerant through corporate proxies. 2) Add client-side retry with resume logic (not trivial for streaming). 3) Configure proxy to allow longer upstream idle or passthrough for our host.

alex: Customer is healthcare regulated — they can't easily change proxy config without security review. They asked for our security docs and KMS info to see if passthrough is feasible.

jen: @alex sent the SOC2/KMS/retention brief earlier: https://redwood.co/security — I'll attach the standard answers. If they need a signed NDA or SOC2 report, we can route through G-Sales.

ops-bot: Support ticket created: SUP-4921 for request r-0a1b2c3d (assigned to eng-streaming).

maria: For immediate triage, ask them to try a backend proxy test (not Electron). Python snippet tends to behave better; use a Session with retries and stream=True.

dan: Snippets to share:
Node TS (enable keepalive):
```js
import http from 'http';
import fetch from 'node-fetch';
const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs: 60000 });
await fetch(url, { agent, headers: { 'Connection': 'keep-alive' } });
```
Python (requests + retry):
```py
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from requests import Session
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
s = Session()
retries = Retry(total=3, backoff_factor=0.5, status_forcelist=[429,502,503,504])
s.mount('http://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
resp = s.post(url, proxies={'http': 'http://proxy:8080'}, stream=True, timeout=(10,60))
for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
    process(chunk)
```

alex: Shared those with the customer. They also reported seeing 429s when their retry storm kicked off. Any guidance for backoff strategy?

maria: Use exponential backoff with jitter. Honor `Retry-After` header on 429s. For POC we can temporarily increase quota to avoid immediate blocks — @saleslead can approve.

alex: @saleslead can we temporarily bump their hosted quota while we triage proxy issues? They are mid-PoC and blocked. Account: `acme-health-567`.

saleslead: Approved a temporary 2x quota for 72h. Please monitor usage and revert if abused.

jen: Ops note — if they want deep packet analysis we'll need their sign-off to capture pcap through their proxy. Also confirm whether proxy does TLS MITM; that will materially affect streaming behavior.

dan: Final triage plan for the customer: 1) Try backend (Python) test with keepalive and retries. 2) If fails, run curl test: `curl -v --http1.1 -N -x http://proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.co/v1/generate` and capture logs. 3) If still failing, provide pcap and we'll run support capture. 4) If proxy cannot be changed, recommend running calls from a small internal service with better proxy policy or route through a dedicated relay that supports streaming.

alex: I'll coordinate steps 1–3 with AcmeHealth and send the curl + snippets. Thanks team :thumbsup:
